title: The Creator Economy: NFTs and Beyond

reader_summary.headline: Welcome to the A16Z podcast, I'm Zorin.
reader_summary.overview: Welcome to the A16Z podcast, I'm Zorin. In today's episode, we're talking about the creator economy and how NFTs, but not just NFTs, are making it possible for artists, musicians, video gamers. And part of that picture is social tokens, which share a crypto foundation with NFTs, but unlike NFTs are typically fungible.

key_points.text: In today's episode, we're talking about the creator economy and how NFTs, but not just NFTs, are making it possible for artists, musicians.
key_points.evidence_quote: In today's episode, we're talking about the creator economy and how NFTs, but not just NFTs, are making it possible for artists, musicians, video gamers, game developers, and writers to create entirely new markets to make money from their work and engage with their fans.

key_points.text: And part of that picture is social tokens, which share a crypto foundation with NFTs, but unlike NFTs are typically fungible.
key_points.evidence_quote: And part of that picture is social tokens, which share a crypto foundation with NFTs, but unlike NFTs are typically fungible, meaning each token has the same value.

key_points.text: You can listen to our explainer episode, All About NFTs.
key_points.evidence_quote: You can listen to our explainer episode, All About NFTs, hosted by Sonal or see our curated NFT Canon on A16Z.com for much more info on NFTs.

key_points.text: But in this episode, we have a hallway style chat featuring A16Z general partner and crypto investor Chris Dixon, talking with Kevin Chu.
key_points.evidence_quote: But in this episode, we have a hallway style chat featuring A16Z general partner and crypto investor Chris Dixon, talking with Kevin Chu, who founded Kabam and is the founder of Rowley, an open network on Ethereum where creators can launch social tokens.

thesis: The episode argues that video gaming models of community engagement and digital assets are propagating from siloed games to the open internet, where NFTs reintroduce scarcity to digital creative work and social tokens provide a digital equivalent to fan club memberships. These assets allow fans to prove their early support, profit from it, and access new experiences, effectively enabling musicians, artists, and writers to monetize their communities in ways previously unavailable.
